what_its_for: Isosorbide dinitrate is used to prevent and treat chest pain (angina) caused by heart disease. It works by relaxing and widening your blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard and gets more blood and oxygen.
how_to_take: Take this medicine exactly as your doctor tells you. Swallow regular tablets whole with a full glass of water. Do NOT crush, chew, or break extended-release (long-acting) capsules or tablets. You may take regular tablets on an empty stomach or with food if your stomach gets upset. Try to take your doses at the same times every day. Do NOT stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this can make your chest pain worse.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you. A common starting dose for regular tablets is 5 to 20 mg taken 2 to 3 times a day. Extended-release forms are usually taken once or twice a day. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose over time. It is important to follow a dosing schedule that gives your body a 'nitrate-free' break of 10 to 14 hours each day (usually overnight) to keep the medicine working properly and prevent your body from getting used to it.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the medicine in a tightly closed container and away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medicine safely — ask your pharmacist about a medication take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can cause a dangerous drop in blood pressure, leading to dizziness or fainting. Do NOT take erectile dysfunction (ED) medicines such as sildenafil (Viagra), tadalafil (Cialis), or vardenafil (Levitra) with this medicine — this combination can cause a sudden, severe, and life-threatening drop in blood pressure. Avoid standing up too quickly from a sitting or lying position to reduce dizziness. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: chest pain that is getting worse or not going away, severe dizziness or fainting, very fast or irregular heartbeat, severe headache that does not go away, blurred vision, shortness of breath, or signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing. Also call your doctor if you feel lightheaded or have frequent headaches that bother you.
when_it_works: Regular tablets start working within 20 to 40 minutes and the effect lasts about 4 to 6 hours. Extended-release forms start working within 30 to 60 minutes and last up to 12 hours. This medicine is mainly used to PREVENT chest pain, not to treat a sudden angina attack already in progress. For a sudden angina attack, use a fast-acting nitroglycerin (sublingual) tablet or spray as directed by your doctor.
special_populations: Older adults may be more sensitive to the blood pressure-lowering effects of this medicine and may have a higher risk of dizziness and falls — use extra caution when standing up. Pregnant or breastfeeding women should talk to their doctor before using this medicine, as its safety has not been fully established. People with low blood pressure, anemia, glaucoma, or recent head injury should use this medicine with caution and only under close medical supervision. Always tell your doctor and pharmacist about all other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you are taking.
